messages.author: 072c955112d6766c
messages.subject: Caught segfault when running getData
parts:
Hi,

When I try to run this code:
meth <- unite(myobj, min.per.group=10L, destrand=TRUE, save.db = TRUE, suffix = "DMS_unite")
myDiff <- calculateDiffMeth(meth, mc.cores=1, covariates=covariates, save.db = TRUE, suffix = "myDiff")
diffMeth <- getMethylDiff(myDiff, difference = 15, qvalue = 0.0125, save.db = TRUE, suffix = "diffMeth")
meth.data <- getData(meth)

I get this error:

*** caught segfault ***

address 0x2afb33c5d1aa, cause 'memory not mapped'

Traceback:

 1: data.table::fread(file = filepath, ...)

 2: fread.gzipped(tbxFile, nrow = nrow, stringsAsFactors = FALSE,     data.table = returnDt, skip = length(Rsamtools::headerTabix(tbxFile)$header))

 3: headTabix(tbxFile = x@dbpath, nrow = x...@num.records, return.type = "data.frame")

 4: getData(meth)

 5: getData(meth)

An irrecoverable exception occurred. R is aborting now ...

/var/spool/slurmd/job34476121/slurm_script: line 10: 128906 Segmentation fault      (core dumped) Rscript 05_dev_methylkit_methylCallingDMS.R

~

Note that I am working with all DB objects and running this on an HPC.

Thanks for your help!

messages.author: 9b48f0bcd1ff214c
messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] Re: Caught segfault when running getData
parts:
This was  an issue for me too.
getData doesn't read the files line by line, so if you use it, it will put all the data into memory and thats the seg fault issue (at least for me it was).
If you can give your HPC job a huge amount of memory you may be able to side-step the problem (but it could be quite wasteful to hold 40GB or more memory when it is only needed for one step in the workflow).
The work around for me was to subset the files outside of R (using awk etc) and then process them in batches (e.g. by chromosome).

Hello Ryan,

I think that the issue is to retrieve the table from big methylDB objects. I have a limited access to huge amount of memory and gave 1To of memory just for the getData() function, but I still have the issue althouth my job used no more than 50GB. I then re-ran the complete analysis without using methylDB object, and the getData() function worked fine. But yes, my job used 500GB, but at least, I can have my complete table to do graphes.
